newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Australian Business News - Oct 4.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Reserve Bank of Australia has warned the Queensland Government that its plans to create a huge financial services group from the planned merger of Suncorp, Queensland Industry Development Corporation and Metway Bank will be closely monitored following the financial nightmares which plagued state-owned banks during the 1980s. Page 1.

Queensland Alumina Ltd has awarded its blue collar workers a 10 percent wage rise through enterprise bargaining at its Gladstone alumina refinery in return for the introduction of annualised salaries and detailed targets for efficiency improvements. Page 3.

University of Southern Queensland's commerce faculty professor Craig Deegan has told a University of New South Wales conference on environmental accounting that corporate environmental reporting is sometimes so low quality it may breach the Corporations Law. Page 20.

Macquarie Bank MBL.AX is helping authorities determine if there was any abnormal trading in options to buy TNT Ltd shares in the lead-up to the A$2 billion friendly takeover by giant Dutch postal and telecommunications group Royal PTT Nederland NV. Page 33.

Tabcorp Holdings' chief executive Ross Wilson will be one of Australia's luckiest top executives if shareholders agree to allocate him another 200,000 shares as part of a five year package that allows him to acquire 500,000 shares at market price with an interest free loan from the company. Page 33.

Department store retailer David Jones is getting ready to storm the expanding home shopping market with an aggressive new campaign that includes a new mail catalogue and CD-ROM system with an Internet service hopefully up and running by Christmas. Page 34.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Shares in chemicals and plastics group ICI Australia Ltd surged to a record high yesterday as speculation mounted that its British parent ICI Plc is to make a A$1 billion-plus move for the remaining 37.8 percent of its Australian off-shoot which it doe not already own. Shares in ICI closed 28 cents higher at A$12.88, marking a rise of 14.5 percent over the past week. Page 21.

The Australian Securities Commission is investigating suspected anomalies in options trading leading up to Wednesday's A$2 billion bid for TNT Ltd by Dutch postal and telecommunications group Royal PTT Nederland NV (KPN). The ASX surveillance unit referred the matter to the ASC after observing possible insider trading movements in the TNT options. Page 21.

David Fewchuk, general manager of industry export assistance project, Australian Concept Car, believes the push by the United States to force Australia to scrap export assistance programmes to the car industry could see the A$1.78 billion export sector overun by imports. Page 21.

Comments by Federal Treasurer Peter Costello that U.S. Federal Reserve chief Dr Alan Greenspan is optimistic about the inflationary outlook, echoed across the world's financial markets again yesterday, pushing Wall Street to an all-time peak and keeping local long-term bond yields at 2.5 year lows. Page 21.

In the first edition of its Property Monitor, Access Economics has revealed the lagging property sector could be in recovery, with almost A$50 billion worth of investment projects either under way or being developed. According to the Monitor, there are 68 projects in the residential, retail, hotel, office and social infrastructure sectors are currently under construction or on the drawing board. Page 22.

David Jones Ltd's managing director Chris Tideman has added to the general pessimism of a bleak Christmas lead-up in the retail sector. Despite noting the coming period will be "extremely tough", Tideman announced the opening of a second David Jones suburban department store in Melbourne's south-east. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD
The Australian Securities Commission is investigating "unusual" trading in transport group TNT in the lead up to Wednesday's A$2 billion takeover bid by a Dutch group.

The A$260 million float of the Papua New Guinea Government's minerals assets in the form of Orogen Minerals will go ahead regardless of the plummet in gold prices and reports of landholders running amok in the PNG highlands. Page 25.

The deal between the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission and Ampol last year which allowed Ampol's A$3 billion merger with Caltex has not produced the promised entry into the market of independent operators and cheaper petrol prices, as indepedent operators are still locked out of the market. Page 25.

The Manager of Meridian Investment Trust, formerly Estate Mortgage Trusts - Tyndall Australia - is confident of winning its A$1 billion damages claim against Burns Philp and eight others, but the lawsuit has already cost Meridian A$15 million and will cost a further A$7 million if the trial goes ahead in February 1997. Page 25.

Stockbroking analysts hold little hope of Amcor posting a net profit that will match last year's performance of A$356 million, with new profit downgrades forecasting annual net profit falls by up to 17 percent this year due to soft paper prices and stiff competition on several fronts. Page 27.

Suncorp may be planning a A$150 to A$200 million property float of its Carindale Shopping Centre in Brisbane, in a move which could boost Australia's depressed retail property market. Sources say Suncorp will retain 50 percent of the units in the single-urpose trust and manage it, with the balance sold to the public. Page 27.
THE AGE

Heavy trading of TNT share options before the announcement of a A$2 billion takeover bid has prompted the Australian Securities Commission investigate for possible evidence of insider trading. ASC officials met surveillance analysts from the ASX yesterday to look at papers detailing unusual transactions in TNT options ahead of the transport groups' takeover announcement. Page 1.
After Foodland Associated posted a 10 percent lower net profit for the year to A$47.3 million from A$52.6 million, it has decided to buy back up to 10 percent of its shares. Page C2.

After more positive bullish sentiment and record-breaking performances on Wall Street yesterday, a rush of late-trade profit-taking has pole-axed the banking sector, with the miners and blue-chips the forces left supporting a limp market. Page C2.

ICI Australia has been questioned by the Australian Stock Exchange while its shares rocketed to an all-time high, amid growing speculation that its U.K. parent ICI Plc is considering restructuring its investment. ICI Australia's managing director Warren Haynes issued a standard reply saying he has no explanation for the shares current surge. Page C2.

A new David Jones store will be the centre piece of the new A$150 million expansion of the Westfield Shoppingtown Fountain Gate near Berwick, which will include a 10-screen Village complex and associated entertainment precinct. But David Jones' chief exective Chris Tideman warned he does not expect any improvement in the flat retail climate this year. Page C3.

With the prospect of the huge injection of cash into the market from the buy-out of TNT, many brokers are looking to see which company will be the next target of an overseas takeover bid, and many agree that Australia has a number of big underperforming industrials which are vulnerable. Page C3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
